title: Sheaves of modules on a scheme have functorial injective embeddings (Stacks 01DI)
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ the abelian category of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules on the underlying topological space of $X$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ has functorial injective embeddings: there are a functor $J:\Mod(\mathcal O_X)\to\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ and a natural transformation $j:\mathrm{id}\to J$ such that for every $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ the morphism $j_{\mathcal F}:\mathcal F\to J(\mathcal F)$ is a monomorphism and $J(\mathcal F)$ is an injective object of $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. In particular, if $I$ is a directed set and $(\mathcal F_i,\varphi_{i'i}:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal F_{i'})_{i\le i'}$ is a system of $\mathcal O_X$-modules over $I$ ($\varphi_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$, $\varphi_{i''i'}\varphi_{i'i}=\varphi_{i''i}$), then $\mathcal I_i=J(\mathcal F_i)$ with $\psi_{i'i}=J(\varphi_{i'i})$ is a system of injective $\mathcal O_X$-modules over $I$, and the monomorphisms $j_{\mathcal F_i}:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal I_i$ satisfy $\psi_{i'i}\circ j_{\mathcal F_i}=j_{\mathcal F_{i'}}\circ\varphi_{i'i}$ for $i\le i'$. (Stacks states and proves this for an arbitrary ringed space.)

source.place: Injectives, Lemma 01DI (label lemma-sheaves-modules-space, line 498), the clause 'In fact it has functorial injective embeddings', and its proof (I(U) = prod_{x in U} J_{O_{X,x}}(F_x), with the functorial injective embedding of modules of More on Algebra, Section injectives-modules); cited in Cohomology, proof of Lemma 01FF (cohomology.tex line 3226). Tag verified in tags/tags: 01DI,injectives-lemma-sheaves-modules-space.

proof.text: *Functorial injective embeddings at the points.* Fix $x\in X$ and put $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$. For an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ the stalk $\mathcal G_x$ is an $R$-module and a morphism $\varphi$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules has an $R$-linear stalk map $\varphi_x$, $s_x\mapsto\varphi_U(s)_x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. The category $\Mod(R)$ is abelian, its monomorphisms are the injective $R$-linear maps [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-enough-injectives], and it is Grothendieck abelian [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-grothendieck-abelian]. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-functorial-injective-embedding] gives a functor $J_x:\Mod(\mathcal O_{X,x})\to\Mod(\mathcal O_{X,x})$ and a natural transformation $j^x:\mathrm{id}\to J_x$ such that for every $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module $M$ the map $j^x_M:M\to J_x(M)$ is injective and $J_x(M)$ is an injective $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module [def-sp-injective-resolutions]; naturality says $J_x(h)\circ j^x_M=j^x_{M'}\circ h$ for every $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-linear $h:M\to M'$. (The source takes for $J_x$ the explicit functor $J_R(M)=(F(M^\vee))^\vee$ of More on Algebra, Lemma 01DD; only the three properties above are used.)

source.place: Injectives, Lemma 01DI (label lemma-sheaves-modules-space, line 498), proof, first sentence; More on Algebra, Lemma 01DD (more-algebra.tex, label lemma-injectives-modules) and the paragraph after it

proof.text: *Skyscrapers of injective modules are injective.* Fix $x$ and an injective $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module $A$. The stalk functor $u:\Mod(\mathcal O_X)\to\Mod(\mathcal O_{X,x})$, $\mathcal G\mapsto\mathcal G_x$, $\varphi\mapsto\varphi_x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] is a functor between abelian categories ([def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-enough-injectives]); it is additive since $(\varphi+\psi)_x(s_x)=(\varphi_U(s)+\psi_U(s))_x=\varphi_x(s_x)+\psi_x(s_x)$, and exact since by [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] (5) a sequence of $\mathcal O_X$-modules exact at the middle term stays exact at the middle term on stalks. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-skyscraper-stalk-adjunction] (1)-(3) the skyscraper functor $A\mapsto i_{x,*}A$ is right adjoint to $u$. Hence $i_{x,*}A$ is an injective object of $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ by [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] [def-sp-injective-resolutions].

source.place: Injectives, Lemma 01DI, proof, second paragraph: 'Hom_{O_{X,x}}(F_x, I_x) = Hom_{O_X}(F, i_{x,*}I_x) ... Hence it is clear that each i_{x,*}I_x is an injective O_X-module (see Homology, Lemma 015Z or argue directly)'; Sheaves, Lemma 009C (sheaves.tex, label lemma-stalk-skyscraper-adjoint)

proof.text: *The object $J(\mathcal F)$.* Let $\mathcal F$ be an $\mathcal O_X$-module. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise], applied to the discrete diagram indexed by the set $X$, the family $(i_{x,*}J_x(\mathcal F_x))_{x\in X}$ has a product $J(\mathcal F)$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ computed on sections, with coordinate projections $p^{\mathcal F}_x:J(\mathcal F)\to i_{x,*}J_x(\mathcal F_x)$; since $(i_{x,*}A)(U)=0$ for $x\notin U$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-skyscraper-stalk-adjunction], $J(\mathcal F)(U)=\prod_{x\in U}J_x(\mathcal F_x)$ with $r\in\mathcal O_X(U)$ acting by $r\cdot(a_x)_x=(r_xa_x)_x$ and restriction to $V\subseteq U$ the projection onto the factors $x\in V$ (the sheaf $\mathcal I$ of the source). Each factor is injective by steps 1 and 2, and $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ is abelian [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so $J(\mathcal F)$ is injective by [lem-weil-pbc-product-injectives].

source.place: Injectives, Lemma 01DI, proof: 'the assignment I : U -> prod_{x in U} J_{O_{X,x}}(F_x) is an abelian sheaf' (Sheaves, Examples 006X, 007R), 'I = prod_{x in X} i_{x,*}I_x is the product of the skyscraper sheaves', 'Hence the injectivity of I follows from Homology, Lemma 0137 (lemma-product-injectives)'

proof.text: *$J$ on morphisms; $J$ is a functor.* (The source asserts functoriality without writing it; here it is.) Let $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ be a morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules. For each $x$, $i_{x,*}(J_x(\varphi_x))\circ p^{\mathcal F}_x:J(\mathcal F)\to i_{x,*}J_x(\mathcal G_x)$ is a morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules ($i_{x,*}$ is a functor by [lem-weil-pbc-module-skyscraper-stalk-adjunction] (1), $\varphi_x$ is $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-linear by [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]), so by the universal property of the product $J(\mathcal G)$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise] there is a unique $J(\varphi):J(\mathcal F)\to J(\mathcal G)$ with $p^{\mathcal G}_x\circ J(\varphi)=i_{x,*}(J_x(\varphi_x))\circ p^{\mathcal F}_x$ for all $x$; on sections $J(\varphi)_U((a_x)_{x\in U})=(J_x(\varphi_x)(a_x))_{x\in U}$. From the formula $\varphi_x(s_x)=\varphi_U(s)_x$ one has $(\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal F})_x=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal F_x}$ and $(\psi\circ\varphi)_x=\psi_x\circ\varphi_x$ (every element of $\mathcal F_x$ is a germ); with the functoriality of $J_x$ (step 1) and of $i_{x,*}$ this gives $p_x\circ J(\mathrm{id})=p_x$ and $p_x\circ J(\psi\circ\varphi)=p_x\circ J(\psi)\circ J(\varphi)$ for all $x$, hence $J(\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal F})=\mathrm{id}_{J(\mathcal F)}$ and $J(\psi\circ\varphi)=J(\psi)\circ J(\varphi)$ by the uniqueness in the universal property. So $J:\Mod(\mathcal O_X)\to\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ is a functor.

source.place: Injectives, Lemma 01DI, statement: 'In fact it has functorial injective embeddings'; the functoriality is left implicit in the proof (written out here, by agent)

proof.text: *The monomorphism $j_{\mathcal F}:\mathcal F\to J(\mathcal F)$.* For each $x$ let $\alpha^x:\mathcal F\to i_{x,*}J_x(\mathcal F_x)$ be the morphism corresponding to the $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-linear map $j^x_{\mathcal F_x}:\mathcal F_x\to J_x(\mathcal F_x)$ under the bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-module-skyscraper-stalk-adjunction] (2): $\alpha^x_U(s)=j^x_{\mathcal F_x}(s_x)$ if $x\in U$, $0$ otherwise. By the universal property of the product [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise] there is a unique $j_{\mathcal F}:\mathcal F\to J(\mathcal F)$ with $p^{\mathcal F}_x\circ j_{\mathcal F}=\alpha^x$; on sections $j_{\mathcal F,U}(s)=(j^x_{\mathcal F_x}(s_x))_{x\in U}$, the canonical map of the source. If $j_{\mathcal F,U}(s)=0$ then $s_x=0$ for all $x\in U$, since each $j^x_{\mathcal F_x}$ is injective (step 1), so $s=0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-sections-determined-by-germs] applied to the underlying sheaf of $\mathcal F$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Thus every $j_{\mathcal F,U}$ is injective, and $j_{\mathcal F}$ is a monomorphism: $j_{\mathcal F}\circ a=j_{\mathcal F}\circ b$ forces $a_U=b_U$ for every open $U$, i.e. $a=b$.

source.place: Injectives, Lemma 01DI, proof: 'There is a canonical map F -> I given by mapping s in F(U) to prod_{x in U} j(s_x) ... This map is injective, see Sheaves, Lemma 0079 (lemma-sheaf-subset-stalks)'

proof.text: *Naturality of $j$.* Let $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$, $U$ open, $s\in\mathcal F(U)$. By steps 4 and 5, the $x$-component ($x\in U$) of $J(\varphi)_U(j_{\mathcal F,U}(s))$ is $J_x(\varphi_x)(j^x_{\mathcal F_x}(s_x))=j^x_{\mathcal G_x}(\varphi_x(s_x))$ (naturality of $j^x$, step 1) $=j^x_{\mathcal G_x}(\varphi_U(s)_x)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], which is the $x$-component of $j_{\mathcal G,U}(\varphi_U(s))$. Two morphisms of $\mathcal O_X$-modules that agree on all sections are equal, so $J(\varphi)\circ j_{\mathcal F}=j_{\mathcal G}\circ\varphi$, i.e. $j:\mathrm{id}\to J$ is a natural transformation.

source.place: Injectives, Lemma 01DI, statement ('functorial injective embeddings'); computation from steps 4-5 (by agent)

proof.text: *Conclusion and the clause on systems.* By steps 3-6, $J$ is a functor, $j:\mathrm{id}\to J$ is natural, each $j_{\mathcal F}$ is a monomorphism and each $J(\mathcal F)$ is injective [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For a directed system $(\mathcal F_i,\varphi_{i'i})$ put $\mathcal I_i=J(\mathcal F_i)$, $\psi_{i'i}=J(\varphi_{i'i})$: functoriality gives $\psi_{ii}=J(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$ and $\psi_{i''i'}\psi_{i'i}=J(\varphi_{i''i'}\varphi_{i'i})=\psi_{i''i}$, so $(\mathcal I_i,\psi_{i'i})$ is a system of injective $\mathcal O_X$-modules, and naturality gives $\psi_{i'i}\circ j_{\mathcal F_i}=j_{\mathcal F_{i'}}\circ\varphi_{i'i}$.
